rules.text: Cold start of a run: `.ygg/bin/egg --mod .ygg/mods/agent-seed --run-id <run-name> --runs-root .ygg/runs --event event.start`.
`--drive stdin` (the default) reads stdin: every step, every proposal acceptance and every gate needs a human-typed index; `q` or end-of-input exits.
`--drive cmd:<path>` does not read stdin: every pending choice goes to the decision command, and the run settles automatically at the ending; a `HUMAN` answer pauses safely (exit 0).
`--drive none` prints the current receipt (including `pendingChoice`) and exits without advancing or reading stdin (exit 0).

`cmd:` must pause on a conflict: print both sides and the note, then exit 0 without choosing a path; after resolving it, rerun the command, or switch to `--drive stdin` and pick 1/2/3 (keep_both / keep_first / revise) from `pendingChoice`.

Decision-command protocol: stdin does not participate; the command receives the path of `decide-input.json` (the full current receipt) as its only argument, and stdout may contain exactly one line — `N` (1..=option count) or `HUMAN[:reason]`.
A 5-second timeout, a non-zero exit, an invalid output or an out-of-range index all fail closed (safe pause, state unchanged); `YGG_DECIDE_CMD` may temporarily override the decision-command path.

Human-action gate (effective when `play.mode=guide`): proposal.accept / gate.approve / coordinate.submit / verify.submit / review.note / `config.set play.mode` may only enter through `ygg.choice_selected`; a direct single-shot `--event` is refused with `[REJECTED:ACTION]` (the envelope stays `ok:true` and the primary state is unchanged). Rejects (gate.reject / proposal.reject) are not restricted — they are the correction channel. So there is exactly one way to accept on a human's behalf: `ygg.choice_selected` (typed by the human, or sent by the agent after reading the receipt).

Never fabricate content: when a job is running but there is no pending proposal, the host does not generate a placeholder proposal (a gate must be satisfied by a real delivery) — it prints a readable reason, pauses safely and exits 0, waiting for an external executor to submit and the command to be rerun.

The runaway guard thresholds come from the Mod's `data/config.json` `drive` section (each field falls back when missing or invalid): the hard step cap is `maxSteps + stepsPerRequirement × requirement count` (fallback 64 + 16×n); a separate stop triggers after `stallLimit` consecutive steps with an unchanged `pendingChoice` (fallback 12).

`play.mode` is Mod narrative semantics, not something the host interprets: `config.set play.mode=<goal|guide>` only switches the Mod's prompts and narrative tone; advancement is driven by `--drive` alone — the host reads neither `play.mode` from `data/config.json` nor `settings.play.mode` from the save KV.

In goal mode the decider is **the agent itself**, not a script and not "always pick 1": under goal the Mod only changes the wording and the prompt tone, advancement still goes through `ygg.choice_selected`, and the agent judges every step from the narrative and the candidates — an acceptance that should be rejected must be rejected, a gate that should wait must wait, and mechanically taking the first item forges a conclusion. The repository ships no default decision script; by design the menu's first item is the main forward action, but it is **not guaranteed to be correct at that step**.
rules.basis: user instruction: the decision belongs to the agent, not to a script

rules.text: Action payloads are JSON strings whose fields are separated by `|`: task.intake `"title|description"`; requirement.add `"title|description[|external_id[|depends_on]]"`; requirement.dispatch `""` / `"0"` (readiness order) / `"rN"` (that requirement only); proposal.submit `"rN|rev|stage|summary|artifacts[|changes[|external_id[|exec=<agent_id>[:<reason>]]]]"`; gate.approve `"rN[|note]"` / `""`; gate.reject `"rN|feedback"` / `""`; verify.submit `"true"` / `"all_green=false;report=…"`; settlement.evolution `"artifact|summary[|c=<kept>/<screened>[|cls=<kind>:<n>,...]][|sessions=<moved>/<remaining>/<destination>][|todo=<remaining>/<verified_by>]"`; settlement.sessions `"moved|remaining|destination"`; settlement.todo `"remaining|verified_by"`; review.note `"lesson|score(1-5)"`. The shape printed in a rejection receipt is the correct format — copy it, never guess a segment position.

requirement.dispatch dispatches by readiness order (draft→plan / planning+plan_ok→development·lane; the legacy planning-without-plan→plan), with a job cap of 4; no candidate or a full slot set is a normal `[DISPATCH] 0 candidates` receipt (idempotent, never counted as a failed step).
A proposal's `changes` reads like `split=a,b` / `merge=r5` / `amend=title:description` / `conflict=r5:note`: a subagent only suggests, and the change lands at `proposal.accept`.

`proposal.accept` accepts exactly one proposal serially and names it with `pN` / `rN`; an empty payload takes the first in requirement-id canonical order — with more than one pending proposal you must name it, otherwise you verify the wrong requirement.

Reject paths: `proposal.reject` → analysis→draft / plan→planning / development→keeps `plan_ok` (not amended → ready, amended → planning); `gate.reject` always stores planning, the plan gate sets `plan_ok` false (a new plan is required) and the accept gate keeps the previous value (not amended → ready, amended → planning).

At acceptance, `rev ≠ req.<i>.rev` → the proposal becomes stale and the requirement gets the stale marker (a readable refusal; an old proposal must never override a newer decision). The recovery path is a new proposal for the same stage at the current rev — such a rebase proposal is accepted only when the requirement has no other pending proposal, and refused otherwise; once the rebase lands the stale marker clears automatically.

An action outside its stage → `[REJECTED:ACTION]`; an invalid payload → `[REJECTED:PAYLOAD]`; an unmet precondition → `[BLOCKED:TODO]`; a human action dispatched single-shot → `[REJECTED:ACTION]`. All four re-render in place (the primary state is unchanged) and all four match `agent.rejectionPrefixes` in `pack.json` (the host reads that to decide "no effect" and does not record a failed step).
